phase: Phase 2 — company tenant mapping and durable projection
summary: The focused tests pass, but the candidate retains an unsafe legacy bypass and does not make durable projection atomic.

findings.title: The legacy constructor bypasses the trusted Company Identity boundary.
evidence: The public constructor accepts { database, mastery } and selects legacy mode without a Company Identity verifier.
The legacy parser checks only structural claims, the Sales audience, the organization key, and a Sales role.
The legacy claim schema accepts any URL issuer and any positive expiration value without checking current time.
An independent runtime probe used an attacker issuer and expiration value 1, then received an applied projection receipt.
The graph found no production caller, but the adapter is exported from both domain barrels and remains publicly callable.
findings.impact: An expired or wrong-issuer claim can mutate Mastery through the public legacy path. This violates the fail-closed identity contract.
findings.required_fix: Expose only the trusted constructor. Require every operation to call the Company Identity verifier and derive the learner scope from its result.

findings.title: Durable Mastery commit and Sales receipt insertion are not atomic.
evidence: ensureBindingAndOutbox commits the mapping and outbox row in one database transaction.
deliverDatabase calls readSnapshot and commitMasteryEvidence after that transaction returns.
insertReceipt uses a separate database insert after the Mastery provider commits.
A crash or receipt failure between those operations leaves Mastery evidence applied without a Sales receipt.
findings.impact: Durable replay and audit state can diverge. Recovery depends on a later retry instead of the required atomic outbox boundary.
findings.required_fix: Use one shared transaction-aware persistence boundary for the Mastery mutation and Sales receipt, or implement an explicit durable handoff protocol.
